questions.stem: What defines an On-Premises IT setup?
options: Servers rented from a provider and accessed over the internet
An organisation buys servers and infrastructure, places them in its own building and manages them with internal teams
Software subscribed to on a monthly basis
Virtual machines provided by a third party
Data stored on employees' personal laptops
questions.explanation: On-Premises means the organisation owns the servers and infrastructure, keeps them in its own location and manages them with its own teams.

questions.stem: What defines Cloud in contrast to On-Premises?
options: Servers owned by the customer but placed in a rented data centre
Software that runs only on mobile devices
Someone else places and manages servers in their own location, and the customer accesses them via the internet
A private network with no internet access
A backup copy kept on external disks
questions.explanation: Cloud is when another party hosts and manages the servers and infrastructure in their building, and the customer accesses them via the internet.

questions.stem: Which event is credited with making Cloud arguably the biggest buzzword in the recent era?
options: The launch of the first smartphone
The Covid-19 pandemic in 2019/20
The introduction of Hadoop
The GDPR regulation
The release of Windows 95
questions.explanation: Cloud became the biggest buzzword after the Covid-19 pandemic, when organisations had to enable Cloud services for employees to keep businesses running.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as something the service provider manages in a Cloud setup?
options: Software upgrades
Disaster Recovery management
High Availability management
Auto-scaling and security
Writing the customer's business strategy
questions.explanation: Cloud centralises compute and storage where software, upgrades, DR, HA, auto-scaling and security are managed by the provider; business strategy is not the provider's job.

questions.stem: In the laptop example from I Am Datapedia!, which situation represents the On-Premises approach?
options: Paying someone else to buy laptops, maintain the software and give you access via the internet
Renting a laptop by the hour
Buying your own laptop, installing and upgrading all software, security, encryption and backups yourself
Borrowing a colleague's laptop
Using a laptop only for email
questions.explanation: Self-managing your own laptop, including software installs, encryption, DR/HA backups and upgrades, is the On-Premises approach; paying someone else to do all that is Cloud.

questions.stem: How is a Private Cloud accessed, compared with a Public Cloud?
options: Private Cloud resides in your premises and is accessible via Intranet; Public Cloud resides somewhere around the globe and is accessible via the Internet
Private Cloud is accessed via the Internet; Public Cloud via Intranet
Both are accessed only via VPN
Private Cloud is accessed by phone line
Public Cloud is only accessible on-site
questions.explanation: A Private Cloud sits in your premises and is reached via Intranet, whereas a Public Cloud sits somewhere around the globe and is reached via the Internet.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the considerations listed before moving data to the Cloud?
options: Whether regulatory bodies in your country allow it, based on the nature of your data
The egress cost of moving data out of the Cloud if you later leave
Whether the provider has all the tools you need or offers third-party tools
Whether you have the internal skill set to support the Cloud services
Whether the provider's data centre has a car park
questions.explanation: The listed considerations are regulation, egress cost, tool availability (and whether as PaaS, SaaS or IaaS) and internal skills.

questions.stem: Why is a major reason given for using Cloud tied to semi and unstructured data?
options: Because 90% of semi and unstructured datasets come from online applications, so it is worth keeping them in the Cloud
Because on-premises storage cannot hold structured data
Because unstructured data is illegal to store on-premises
Because Cloud data is automatically structured
Because unstructured data needs no processing
questions.explanation: Since about 90% of semi and unstructured data comes from online applications, it makes sense to take it straight to the Cloud rather than download it on-premises.

questions.stem: How much data is Twitter alone said to generate daily?
options: 52 GB
5 TB
52 TB
520 TB
52 PB
questions.explanation: As per the stats quoted, Twitter itself generates 52 TB of data daily, which is why such data is best taken directly to the Public Cloud.

questions.stem: Which Cloud service type is described as 'kind of SaaS'?
options: IaaS
CaaS
PaaS
DaaS
FaaS
questions.explanation: DaaS (Data as a Service) is noted as a kind of SaaS, while AAaaS is a kind of PaaS and SaaS.
